lesson.title: 4.10 What Time Is It?
lesson.unit_outcome: Say where people and things are at home, describe a short daily routine, ask and answer Do you...? questions, and say the day and the time.
lesson.goal: Identify morning, afternoon, evening and night from contextual scenes, then ask and answer the time, read whole hours and distinguish a.m. from p.m.
lesson.grammar_function: It is morning/afternoon/evening/night; What time is it? It is + number + o'clock; in the morning / in the afternoon / in the evening / at night; It is + number + a.m./p.m. No routines or activity-at-time statements.
lesson.prerequisite: Units 2–3 numbers 1–12, it/is; 4.3 in/the; 4.5 in the morning. No routine verbs are required.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Name the part of the day, take both roles in a time exchange and give a clear whole-hour answer with its day period.

models.text: It is seven o'clock in the morning.
It is three o'clock in the afternoon.
It is seven o'clock in the evening.
It is nine o'clock at night.

approval.evidence: The user approved the revised local HTML proposal after requesting dedicated clock-free day-part images first, followed by a two-person time question and a close-up of the same clock with the full reply. Existing useful contextual clock originals are restored. No image API or generation service is authorized.
approval.allocation_note: 70 purposeful cards: four dedicated day-part cards at the beginning of each of the five stages, plus the retained 50 time cards. Allocation: 18 Learn, 14 Recognize, 14 Listen, 12 Speak, 12 Use. All hours 1–12 and both conversational roles remain.
approval.media_status: The approved lesson design is implemented in this source. Exact two-person pointing photos and same-clock response shots remain a separate required media gate; existing asking bindings are temporary, never evidence of approved continuity.
